sections.h2: Where do Columbus County property tax bills get paid?
sections.html:
The Columbus County Tax Office collects at 810 Pinckney Street in Whiteville, and the public lobby keeps hours from half past eight to five The main tax office number is 910-640-6635, and the mailing address is P.O. Box 1468, Whiteville, NC 28472.

The county's collections page lists payment by mail, phone, online, dropbox or in person. Online payment runs through columbus.webtaxpay.com, and the phone line is 877-768-4775. Cash, check and credit card are all taken.

The collections page says the office collects for more than the county. It names the City of Whiteville and the towns of Fair Bluff, Sandyfield, Boardman, Brunswick, Cerro Gordo, Bolton, Chadbourn, Tabor City and Lake Waccamaw. For older years the page sends inquiries about some towns to the towns themselves, so call town hall if you cannot find an old balance.

sections.h2: What is the Columbus County property tax rate?
sections.html:
Columbus County sets $0.805 per $100 of assessed valuation for fiscal year 2026-2027, with all of it going to the General Fund. Commissioners adopted the budget ordinance on June 1, 2026.

The ordinance bases that rate on an estimated total valuation of $4,010,748,958 and a collection rate of 97.72 percent, and it says discounts will be allowed for early payment. Public schools are funded through two systems, Columbus County Schools and Whiteville City Schools. The ordinance also levies a special fire tax by district on top of the county rate.

sections.h2: When did Columbus County last revalue, and when is the next one?
sections.html:
The last revaluation was in 2021, and the county's budget message to commissioners in May 2026 says the next one is not until 2029.

The same message explains why that timing matters. It says property tax revenue stays relatively flat except in revaluation years and that the county collects roughly $30 million a year. A seller in Columbus County is therefore likely to see an assessed value that was set in 2021. The Census Bureau's median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $146,000; ask the appraisal staff how your parcel was valued if your own figure looks far from that.

sections.h2: What are the Columbus County payment deadlines and late charges?
sections.html:
Payment is due September 1, and January 5 is the last day before delinquency. The county's collections page says amounts are good through the last day of the month and that interest of three-fourths of 1 percent accrues on the first day of each month on delinquent taxes.

State law adds a 2 percent charge from January 6 to February 1, under G.S. 105-360. Mailed payments count as received on the USPS postmark date.

Once a parcel has been advertised for sale, only certified funds are accepted to redeem it. The county's page says that once a sale is confirmed by the court there is no redemption in North Carolina. To find out whether a property is in tax foreclosure proceedings, the tax collector's office invites you to contact it directly.

sections.h2: How does a tax foreclosure sale work in Columbus County?
sections.html:
Sales are held outside the main entrance of the Columbus County Courthouse unless the weather is bad. The county's foreclosures page says the notice posted at the courthouse and printed in the newspaper controls, and the page itself is only an informal list of answers.

  • The high bidder must pay a deposit of 20 percent of the bid or $750, whichever is greater. On sales over $5,000 a $1,000 cash deposit is due immediately, with the rest within two business days.
  • Every bid is open to a 10-day upset period, and upset bids are filed through the Clerk of Court with a 5 percent or $750 deposit, whichever is greater.
  • After the upset period ends and the sale is confirmed, the last high bidder has three days to pay the balance to the commissioner.
  • The owner keeps the property until a new deed is recorded and may redeem it until the court confirms the sale.

Upset bid amounts are found through the NC eCourts portal with the full file number, and the form to bid is AOC-CV-414. The clerk will not answer upset bid questions by phone or fill out the form for you.

sections.h2: What property tax relief does Columbus County offer?
sections.html:
The county posts an application for the elderly and disabled exclusion, and the state also offers a disabled veteran exclusion and a circuit breaker deferral. Filing opens January 1 and closes June 1, and one program per owner is the limit.

  • County application page (2025 tax year): household income at or under $37,900, status as 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled on January 1, and a permanent residence titled in the applicant's exact name.
  • State figures for the 2026 tax year: the income ceiling rises to $38,800, and the amount excluded is whichever is bigger, $25,000 or half the appraised value.
  • Disabled veterans: $45,000 of appraised value is excluded, with no age or income test, using Form NCDVA-9.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4 percent of income up to the limit, 5 percent above it up to 150 percent of the limit.

The county asks for the prior year's income tax statement, an SSA-1099, a doctor's certification for applicants under 65 and a death certificate where a spouse has died and the deed was not corrected. It says applications are denied if they are incomplete, if the name on the deed does not match the application or if they miss the deadline. The county notes that an approved elderly or disabled application does not have to be repeated every year unless household circumstances or income change; the state says a circuit breaker application is filed anew each year.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Columbus County assessment?
sections.html:
Talk to the appraisal staff first; if that fails, the next forum is the county's equalization board. State law makes the commissioners that board unless a special one is created, so ask who sits on Columbus County's.

The board opens its session between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May. In an ordinary year it wraps up by the third Monday after that first meeting and generally cannot sit beyond July 1. A hearing request, in writing or in person, must arrive before adjournment, or within 15 days of a late-mailed notice. Rulings are mailed within 30 days.

Beyond that sits the Property Tax Commission, which has a 30-day filing window running from the board's mailing date. Personal property such as vehicles and equipment is handled by separate staff at the tax office.

sections.h2: What else is on a Columbus County title search that affects a sale?
sections.html:
The county tax office page reproduces a state notice, Session Law 2018-113 and G.S. 106-741, about farm proximity. Land records must carry a notice alerting a person researching title that a tract lies within one-half mile of a poultry, swine or dairy qualifying farm or a voluntary agricultural district, or within 600 feet of any other qualifying farm.

The same page lists staff for the solid waste trash user fee and for senior citizen exemptions, so ask the tax office whether any trash fee is attached to a parcel before closing. Columbus County covers 938.12 square miles of land with about 54 people per square mile, so farm and rural parcels are common and the notice is worth reading.

sections.h2: What is the Columbus County housing stock like?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts estimates 50,487 residents for July 2025 and 23,724 housing units. Population was 58,098 in 2010 and 50,623 in 2020.

Homeowners occupy 71.1 percent of housing, valued at a median $146,000, while renters pay a median gross $824 (2020 to 2024). A typical household earns $49,442 a year, and the poverty rate is 19.3 percent. Only 55 building permits were issued in 2025, and veterans number 2,668.

faqs.q: What is the Columbus County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The adopted fiscal year 2026-2027 county rate is $0.805 per $100 of assessed value. Fire district taxes range from 0.06 to 0.12 per $100, and city or town taxes are billed separately.

faqs.q: When are Columbus County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1 is the due date, and January 5 is the last day to pay before interest begins, which then builds at three-fourths of 1 percent a month after the initial January 6 charge.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Columbus County property taxes in person?
faqs.a: Pay at the Columbus County Tax Office, 810 Pinckney Street, Whiteville. Staff serve the public lobby from half past eight until five, and you can also pay by mail, by phone at 877-768-4775, online or at the dropbox.

faqs.q: When is the next Columbus County revaluation?
faqs.a: The county's May 2026 budget message says the next revaluation is not until 2029. The previous revaluation was in 2021.

faqs.q: Can I stop a Columbus County tax foreclosure?
faqs.a: An owner can redeem until the court confirms the sale, by paying the taxes, interest and costs. After advertising, the county takes certified funds only.
